The accused No.1 to 3 have received the above Pal Chand Jain vs Ayub Ahamed Khan Alias Ayub on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50893672/
2 amount from C.W.1 to 5 from 01/09/2014 to 24/12/2014, by executing an agreement in favour of C.W.1 to 5 and issued cheques in their favour with respect to said amount, pertaining to his account No.0011396062 of Kotak C.C.No.23662/2017 Mahindra Bank, by putting false signature on the said cheques.

On the basis of first information statement lodged by the complainant, a case is registered against the accused No.1 to 3, for the offence punishable U/Sec.420, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of I.P.C.
Accordingly, the investigation officer has conducted investigation in the case and filed the final report against the accused No.1 to 3, for the above alleged offences.
4. On receipt of prosecution papers, the cognizance of above offence is taken against the accused No.1 to 3 and summons were issued to them.
Accordingly, the accused No.1 C.C.No.23662/2017 to 3 have appeared in the case through their counsel and obtained bail.
In compliance of Sec.207 of Cr.P.C., the prosecution papers were supplied to the accused persons.
Thereafter, charge for the offence punishable U/Sec.420, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of I.P.C., is framed, read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 3 in the language known to them.

The accused No.1 to 3 have denied the charge,
pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5. In order to substantiate its case and to bring home the guilt of the accused persons, the prosecution has examined total three witnesses as P.W.1 to 3 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.P.1 to 4.
After closure of prosecution evidence, the statement of accused No.1 to 3 as contemplated U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C., is recorded and read over to them.
The accused No.1 to 3 have denied all the incriminating circumstances appearing against them in the prosecution evidence and stated no evidence in their defence.
6. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material available on record.

The following points arise for my consideration:
POINTS 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 01/09/2024,
at house No.23/1, 4th T Block, 11th A Main Road, 36th A Cross, Jayanagar,
Bengaluru, the accused No.1 to 3, in furtherance of common intention, by giving false assurance of giving double returns in a year and 12.5% service charges on investing Pal Chand Jain vs Ayub Ahamed Khan Alias Ayub on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50893672/
3 money for purchasing new machinery for their Sapphire Honda Service Station,
induced C.W.1 to 5 to invest an amount of Rs.15,10,000/- from 01/09/2014 to 24/12/2024, and thereafter they have neither paid any returns to C.W. 1 to 5, nor they have refunded their invested amount and cheated them and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec.420 R/w Sec.34 of I.P.C. ?
2.

sentences.text: It is specific case of the prosecution that, the accused No.1 to 3, by giving false assurance of providing double returns in a year and 12.5% service charges on investment of money for purchasing new machinery for their Sapphire Honda Service Station, have induced C.W.1 to 5 to invest an amount of Rs.15,10,000/-, from 01/09/2014 to 24/12/2014.
Thereafter, the accused No.1 to 3 have neither paid any returns to C.W.1 to 5, nor they have refunded their invested amount and thereby cheated them.

Further, it is alleged that, C.C.No.23662/2017 on 27/02/2017 at 06:18 p.m., when C.W.1 phone called the accused No.1 and demanded to repay their amount, the accused No.1 to 3 have abused him in filthy language and gave life-threat to them.
12. But, none of the alleged victims i.e. C.W.1 to 5 have appeared before the Court and stepped into witness box to depose their case.
Even after repeated issuance of summons and warrant to the said witnesses, the prosecution has failed to secure and examine the said witnesses.
In such circumstances, the very contents of Ex.P.2 first information statement and the statements of C.W.2 to 5 have remained unproved in the case.
The learned counsel for accused during his arguments submitted that, the matter has been compromised out of Court between the alleged victims and the accused persons.
Hence, they did not bother to appear before the Court for recording their evidence.

When the alleged victims themselves have not appeared to the Court and depose their case on oath,
the evidence of other witnesses on record will not serve any purpose to the case of prosecution or in proving the charges leveled against the accused persons.

On account of non-examination of the alleged victims in the case, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the accused No.1 to 3 have induced C.W.1 to 5 to invest Rs.15,10,000/- for purchasing machinery for their Sapphire Honda Service Station, by giving false assurance of providing double returns in a year and 12.5% service charges on invested money and cheated them.
Further, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, on 27/02/2017 at 06:18 p.m., the accused No.1 to 3 have abused C.W.1 to 5 in filthy language or gave life-threat to them.

14. On meticulously going through the contents of first information statement and the statements of other witnesses recorded before the investigation officer, it clearly goes to show that, on account of non-payment of returns as promised by the accused persons and even not refunding their amount,
the C.W.1 to 5 have approached the Police and initiated criminal proceedings against accused persons for recovery of said amount.

The alleged victims in the case, instead of filing a civil suit against the accused persons for recovery of money, they have opted to initiate criminal proceedings against them with a sole intention to recover the said amount.

The Hon'ble Apex C.C.No.23662/2017 Court in series of cases has held that, the mere inability of the accused to return the borrowed amount cannot give rise to criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction, as it is mens-rea which is the crux of offence punishable under Sec.420 of I.P.C.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in case S. N.
Palanitkar and others V/S State of Bihar and another, reported in AIR 2001 SC 2960, has clearly held that, "In order to constitute an offence of cheating, the intention to deceive should be in existence at the time when the inducement was made.

sentences.text:
It is necessary to show that, person had fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making the promise, to say that he committed an act Pal Chand Jain vs Ayub Ahamed Khan Alias Ayub on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50893672/
5 of cheating.

entities.text: Pal Chand Jain vs Ayub Ahamed Khan Alias Ayub
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A mere failure to keep up promise subsequently cannot be presumed as an act leading to cheating".

15. It is not the case of prosecution in the present case that, the accused No.1 to 3 were having fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of receiving the alleged amount from C.W.1 to 5 or at the time of executing the alleged agreement by the accused persons in their favour.

As per the contents of first information statement of C.W.1 and the statements of C.C.No.23662/2017 other victims i.e. C.W.2 to 5, recorded before the investigation officer, after investing the amount the accused persons have paid some amount to them, but they have not paid the amount as promised by them or as per the agreed terms.
If the accused No.1 to 3 had fraudulent or dishonest intention to dupe the amount of C.W.1 to 5, they would have not paid any amount to them.
There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that.
the accused No.1 to 3 were having fraudulent or dishonest intention to deceive C.W.1 to 5 right from the beginning of the transaction in between them.

16. Therefore, for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges leveled against the accused No.1 to 3, beyond all reasonable doubt.
As such, the accused No.1 to 3 are entitled for acquittal.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 to 3 in Negative.

17. Point No.4: In view of above conclusion, I proceed to pass the following order:
C.C.No.23662/2017 ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 to 3 are acquitted for the offence punishable U/Sec.420, 504 & 506 R/w Sec.34 of I.P.C.
The bail bond and surety bond executed by the accused No.1 to 3 and their sureties stands canceled.
